transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what brought me in is that... some evenings after work, I end up eating just way more than I ever meant to. 

It seems to happen especially when I've been really strict with what I eat all day. I'll sit down and have my regular dinner, but then... I just keep going. I'll eat bowls of cereal, crackers, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and then sweets, all packed into just a couple of hours. It's been bothering me enough that I figured I should come in and talk to someone about it.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever do anything to try to compensate for the calories, such as making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't ever make myself throw up or take laxatives or anything like that. But I do try to make up for it. 

Usually, the next day after one of those nights, I'll tell myself I'm balancing it out by skipping breakfast and lunch entirely. Or I'll go take an extra-long hike... or just push myself a lot harder at softball conditioning, even when I'm really tired. I just feel like I have to do something to work off all that extra food from the night before.
During those times when you are eating those large amounts of food, do you feel like you are unable to stop or that you cannot control what or how much you are eating?

Yeah, I do. Once I get started on those nights, it's like... I just keep going back to the kitchen. Even while I'm standing there telling myself to stop, I just keep eating. I don't really feel like I'm back in charge of myself until I'm just uncomfortably full.
How do you feel emotionally after these episodes of overeating?

Honestly, I just feel... pretty awful. I get really mad at myself. Um, I guess guilty is the best word for it. I just sit there feeling bad that I let it happen again, especially after trying to be so strict during the day. It's just really frustrating.
How much does your body shape or weight influence how you feel about yourself as a person?

It influences me quite a bit, honestly. Like, if I'm getting dressed for work and my waistband feels tight before a client luncheon, or maybe a leadership meeting... I just start feeling like I look sloppy. I start worrying that people won't take me as seriously. And I mean, I know I've still been doing my job well and taking care of my clients, but... yeah, how my clothes fit and my weight just really dictate how confident I feel about myself as a person.
